title: Normal standby - no faults
shortDescription: Single LED flash means the integrated control board is healthy and waiting for a thermostat call.
fullDescription:
Nordyne (parent of Maytag, Frigidaire, Westinghouse, Tappan, Gibson and Philco HVAC) uses a common control board family. A slow, steady single flash on the diagnostic LED reports a healthy board waiting for a heat or cool call.

If the furnace will not start despite the 1-flash code, look upstream: thermostat, batteries, low-voltage wiring, the door safety switch, or a tripped 3 A fuse on the board.
safetyWarning: Even at idle, line voltage is present at the control board terminals. Switch off the disconnect before opening the blower door.

causes.cause: Thermostat not closing R-W (dead batteries, wiring)

fixSteps.title: Verify thermostat call
fixSteps.instruction: Set thermostat 5 F above room temp; listen for click and look for 24 V at R-W.

fixSteps.title: Check door switch
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm the blower door is fully seated, depressing the safety switch.

whenToCallPro: If 24 V is at the board with W energized but the inducer never starts, have a tech load-test the board.

faq.a: Yes - Maytag/Westinghouse/Tappan furnaces share Nordyne boards and codes.

title: Pressure switch closed when it should be open
shortDescription: Inducer is off but pressure switch shows closed - stuck switch or wiring fault.
fullDescription:
Two flashes mean the IFC saw the pressure switch closed before the inducer was commanded to start. This is a critical safety check - a closed switch with no inducer running suggests a stuck switch or a jumper across the contacts.

The board will not allow ignition until the switch opens (de-energized state) at start of cycle.
safetyWarning: Bypassing the pressure switch can let the burners light into a blocked flue, causing CO to spill into the home.

fixSteps.title: Power off
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect at the service switch.

fixSteps.title: Test switch at rest
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect leads; ohm the terminals. Should be OPEN (no continuity) at rest.

fixSteps.title: Replace if closed
fixSteps.instruction: If continuity reads, replace the switch with the OEM part number.

whenToCallPro: If switch tests open but the code persists, have a tech inspect the IFC.

faq.a: Years of pressure cycling and condensate corrosion fuse contacts together.

title: Pressure switch failed to close
shortDescription: Inducer is running but the pressure switch never closed - venting, drain, or inducer issue.
fullDescription:
Three flashes mean the inducer started but the pressure switch did not close in time. The IFC will retry up to 3 times before locking out for an hour.

On 80% AFUE Nordyne furnaces, the most common causes are flue blockage, a torn pressure-switch hose, or a weak inducer motor. On 90%+ condensing models, a clogged condensate trap is the #1 cause - water backs up into the inducer housing and prevents draft.
safetyWarning: Do not bypass the switch - flue blockage can spill CO into the home.

fixSteps.title: Inspect vent terminal
fixSteps.instruction: Look outside for snow, leaves, or insect screen blockage at the PVC vent.

fixSteps.title: Clean condensate trap
fixSteps.instruction: Remove the trap, flush with warm water and bleach solution.

fixSteps.title: Inspect hose
fixSteps.instruction: Pull the silicone hose at the inducer port and check for water, kinks, cracks.

whenToCallPro: Inducer replacement is best handled by a technician.

faq.q: How do I know if condensate is the issue?
faq.a: Pull the silicone hose at the inducer - if water dribbles out, the trap is plugged.

title: Open high-temperature limit switch
shortDescription: The primary limit opened due to overheating in the heat exchanger.
fullDescription:
Four flashes indicate the high-temperature limit safety switch on the heat exchanger has opened. Burners shut off, blower runs to cool the exchanger.

Root cause is restricted airflow 95% of the time: dirty filter, closed registers, undersized return, or failed blower. A repeated 4-flash code that returns after airflow correction may indicate a cracked heat exchanger.
safetyWarning: Repeated limit trips on a clean system can indicate a cracked heat exchanger - a CO hazard requiring professional inspection.

fixSteps.title: Replace filter
fixSteps.instruction: Install clean OEM-spec filter.

fixSteps.title: Open registers
fixSteps.instruction: Verify all supply registers are fully open and unblocked.

fixSteps.title: Measure temp rise
fixSteps.instruction: Should be within nameplate range, typically 35-65 F.

whenToCallPro: If repeated trips after airflow is restored.

faq.q: Can I replace the limit switch?
faq.a: Replacement won't fix the underlying airflow problem - the new switch will trip too.

title: Flame roll-out switch open
shortDescription: The manual-reset roll-out switch tripped - flames or hot gas exited the burner box.
fullDescription:
Five flashes indicate the flame roll-out switch (mounted at the front of the burner box) opened due to flames or excess heat escaping forward. This is a serious safety event requiring professional diagnosis.

Common causes: blocked flue, cracked or rusted heat exchanger, failed inducer (no draft), or heavy soot buildup blocking the burner-to-exchanger path.
safetyWarning: Flame roll-out indicates combustion gases are not flowing correctly through the heat exchanger and CO can enter the home. Stop using the furnace until inspected.
symptoms: Smell of combustion in equipment room

fixSteps.title: Stop using furnace
fixSteps.instruction: Turn off gas at appliance shutoff. Verify CO alarms are working.

fixSteps.title: Schedule professional inspection
fixSteps.instruction: Heat exchanger must be inspected with borescope and combustion analyzer.

whenToCallPro: Always - this is a CO hazard.

faq.q: Can I just reset the switch?
faq.a: Never reset without finding the cause - you risk fire or CO poisoning.

title: Reverse line voltage polarity
shortDescription: Hot and neutral are swapped at the furnace, or chassis ground is missing.
fullDescription:
Six flashes indicate reversed L1/N polarity or absent ground on the 120 VAC supply. The flame sensing circuit needs proper polarity and ground to detect the small flame current.

Correct at the disconnect or service panel; do not bypass.
safetyWarning: Reversed polarity can energize the chassis - shock hazard. Hire an electrician if you are unsure.
symptoms: Burner lights then drops out on flame sense

fixSteps.title: Test with receptacle tester
fixSteps.instruction: Plug into outlet at the disconnect (if cord-and-plug furnace) - 3 lights tell you what's wrong.

fixSteps.title: Multimeter check
fixSteps.instruction: Hot-Neutral 120 V, Hot-Ground 120 V, Neutral-Ground ~0 V.

fixSteps.title: Correct wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Hire electrician to swap conductors at the panel/disconnect.

faq.a: Flame sense uses earth ground as the return path for a tiny rectified current.

title: Weak / lost flame signal
shortDescription: Flame is established but flame current is below the 1.5 microamp minimum.
fullDescription:
Seven flashes mean the burner lit but the IFC didn't read enough flame current to confirm flame. After three trials it locks out.

90% of fixes are simply cleaning the flame sensor rod with fine emery cloth or scotch pad. Other causes: cracked porcelain insulator, dirty burners, low gas pressure, missing ground.
safetyWarning: Always shut off gas and power before pulling the burner assembly.
symptoms: Flame lights for 2-4 seconds then shuts off

fixSteps.title: Power and gas off
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect electrical and close gas valve.

fixSteps.title: Clean flame sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Remove sensor (1 screw), polish rod with 320-grit emery cloth or non-abrasive scotch pad.

fixSteps.title: Reinstall and test
fixSteps.instruction: Restore power/gas; flame current should read 2-6 microamps.

whenToCallPro: If cleaning and replacing the sensor doesn't fix the code.

faq.q: Can I use steel wool to clean it?
faq.a: No - steel wool leaves conductive fragments. Use emery cloth or scotch pad.

title: Ignition failure - no flame
shortDescription: Igniter fired and gas valve opened but no flame was detected.
fullDescription:
Eight flashes mean the IFC ran a complete ignition trial but never sensed flame. Three trials, then 1-hour lockout.

Most frequent cause is a cracked hot-surface igniter, followed by spider webs in burner orifices, low gas pressure, or a closed manual gas valve.
safetyWarning: If you smell gas during a failed ignition, leave the building and call the gas utility.

causes.cause: Closed manual gas valve / empty propane tank

fixSteps.title: Verify gas supply
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm shutoff is open; verify other gas appliances run.

fixSteps.title: Inspect igniter
fixSteps.instruction: Look for cracks or white powder. Cold resistance should be 40-90 ohms.

fixSteps.title: Clean burners
fixSteps.instruction: Vacuum and brush away spider webs and rust flakes.

whenToCallPro: Manifold pressure or gas valve testing.

faq.q: How long do hot-surface igniters last?

title: Failed flame sense after lockout
shortDescription: Flame was sensed when it should not be present (gas valve closed) - latching fault.
fullDescription:
Nine flashes on Nordyne furnaces indicate the flame signal was detected when the gas valve was de-energized. This is a safety latch - it usually points to a stuck gas valve leaking gas, or a flame sensor reading a reflection or hot surface as flame.

This code requires power-cycling and full diagnosis before resuming service.
safetyWarning: A leaking gas valve can release gas with no flame to consume it. Shut off gas immediately and call a tech.

fixSteps.title: Shut off gas
fixSteps.instruction: Close manual gas valve immediately.

fixSteps.title: Call licensed HVAC tech
fixSteps.instruction: This is not a DIY-safe diagnosis.

faq.q: Can I bypass and run anyway?

title: Gas valve / igniter wiring fault
shortDescription: IFC detected open or shorted output to the gas valve or hot-surface igniter.
fullDescription:
Ten flashes indicate the IFC measured an open or shorted output on either the gas valve coil drive or the hot-surface igniter circuit. The board protects itself with an hour lockout.

Most commonly a melted spade terminal or a cracked igniter that has gone open. Less frequently the IFC's output triac itself has failed.
safetyWarning: Shut off gas before disconnecting valve wires. Verify valve is fully closed before re-energizing.
symptoms: No igniter glow OR no gas response

fixSteps.title: Power and gas off
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect electrical service and close gas shutoff.

fixSteps.title: Inspect spade terminals
fixSteps.instruction: Check both gas valve and igniter spades for melting or corrosion. Replace burnt connectors.

fixSteps.title: Test igniter resistance
fixSteps.instruction: 40-90 ohms cold; open = replace.

whenToCallPro: Gas valve replacement requires a licensed technician.

faq.q: Can I substitute generic gas valves?
faq.a: Use only the OEM or AGA-listed equivalent. Cross-brand valves may have wrong pressure regulator.
